newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi sees higher earnings in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sappi sees higher earnings in 1997.

text.p: South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd said on Wednesday that its earnings per share for the current full year should be more than the 230 cents recorded in 1996, provided there is no further deterioration of market conditions.
Sappi chairman Eugene van As told the firm's annual general meeting that depressed pulp prices were hitting the industry.
"Paper markets continue to be uncertain and strong demand is not reflected in price increases, mainly because of depressed pulp prices," he said.
He added that the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against the German mark and the Japanese yen was also creating a confusing picture for pulp prices.
Van As warned that pulp price rises, which had been expected around March this year, have now been delayed and the price may even dip down in the short term.

However, he said that overall pulp prices are in a rising trend over the next two years. "While the immediate prospects are still uncertain, we see pulp and paper prices to be in a rising trend over the long term," he said.
The firm has also been hit by industrial unrest, especially in Swaziland where a political strike closed the firm's Usutu Pulp unit for a month at a cost of one million rand in sales a day.
"Taking all these adverse factors into account we can expect a level of earnings for the first half of the year to reflect only a small increase on the second half of last year," he said.
He also warned that, despite a prediction of a rise in earnings for the full year, the internal budget established by the company will not be achieved in current conditions.
Sappi shares were down 50 cents to 35.00 rand at 1230 GMT.
